title: The Evidence Ladder for Reinforcement Learning in Healthcare: From Retrospective Policies to Trusted Interventions
abstract: arXiv:2609.23374v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a natural language for healthcare decisions whose conse- quences unfold over time, yet most reported progress remains far from routine intervention. Ex- isting surveys organize the field by algorithm or clinical application. We instead review healthcare RL through an evidence ladder: problem formulation, retrospective identification, policy estima- tion, stress testing, prospective evaluation, and lifecycle monitoring. This view connects clinical treatment, patient engagement, and health-system operations while exposing a recurring gap: evi- dence that a policy scores well in a historical dataset is not evidence that it will improve care. We synthesize the assumptions and failure modes at each rung, identify what evidence can and can- not transfer across settings, and propose reporting practices for cumulative evaluation. Restless bandits are included as one special case, not as the organizing framework

translated_title: 医疗保健中强化学习的证据阶梯：从回顾性策略到可信干预
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）为那些后果随时间逐步显现的医疗决策提供了一种自然的建模语言，然而大多数已报道的进展仍远未达到常规临床干预的水平。现有的综述通常按算法或临床应用来组织该领域，而我们则通过一个“证据阶梯”来审视医疗强化学习：问题建模、回顾性识别、策略估计、压力测试、前瞻性评估和生命周期监测。这一视角将临床治疗、患者参与和医疗系统运营联系起来，同时揭示了一个反复出现的鸿沟：策略在历史数据集中得分良好的证据，并不等于它能够真正改善医疗护理的证据。我们综合了阶梯每一级上的假设和失效模式，识别了哪些证据可以在不同场景间迁移、哪些不能，并提出了用于累积评估的报告实践。不安分老虎机作为其中一个特例被纳入讨论，而非作为组织全文的框架。
tldr: 该论文提出用“证据阶梯”框架（从问题建模、回顾性识别到前瞻性评估与生命周期监测）来审视医疗强化学习，核心观点是策略在历史数据上的高分并不等于能改善真实医疗护理，并系统总结了每一级的假设、失效模式及累积评估的报告规范。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an "evidence ladder" framework for healthcare reinforcement learning—spanning problem formulation, retrospective identification, policy estimation, stress testing, prospective evaluation, and lifecycle monitoring—arguing that strong performance on historical data does not guarantee improved care, while synthesizing assumptions, failure modes, and cumulative evaluation reporting practices at each rung.
